Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

we would like the maintainer to tell us which reports already exist and whether the import date in those reports uses the computer clock or the date recorded by the camera that distinction matters because the computer clock was set incorrectly for eleven days in october last year the family corrected the folder labels by hand but nobody wrote down which files were affected i am not asking for a reconstruction of that period i only want to know whether a new batch report would make the chosen date source visible and whether an uncertain camera date can be marked without changing the image metadata

finally please keep the discussion focused on this importer and the next family archive run mara is available on tuesday evening and joel can join after seven but neither of them can test a new version before the weekend if the maintainer needs a sample folder we can provide a copy of the 2021 picnic folder with names and dates as they currently appear it contains fifty eight photographs and two short videos and should not be used as a reason to reorganize the originals we would like a clear list of what can be checked on saturday what information is still missing and which questions need an answer from us before anyone changes the importer", "output": "I am asking for help maintaining the family photo importer that my aunt Mara and I use for the Keller family archive. It runs on a small computer in her dining room and copies pictures from phones, memory cards, and two older laptops into one dated folder tree. Joel, my cousin, checks the folders with her, but he does not change the importer itself. On Friday—no, sorry, on Saturday—we are planning to review the next import before Mara scans the envelopes from her parents' house. I want the instructions to reflect how we actually work and not assume that every picture has a date or a readable filename.

Mara usually brings home one card with about 400 images from a family gathering, and Joel connects it after dinner. The importer creates a folder for the year, then a folder for the month, and keeps each original filename when that name is usable. Last month, we had 37 files called image001 because two phones and one camera had reused the same names. The importer added a short device suffix to those copies, but we need to check that the suffix stays attached when the files are moved from the incoming folder into the dated folders. I do not know whether the older laptop exports will include the same camera information as the phones.

Please ask the maintainer to check the duplicate handling without deleting or renaming any original files. The importer should still make a separate review list when two pictures have the same date and nearly identical sizes, because they might be copies, but Mara sometimes takes a still photo and a burst frame a few seconds apart. She wants those left for a person to compare, not automatically merged. Joel said, “Last time the review list was clear until the card reader disconnected, and then we could not tell which batch it described.” Could the batch name include the card label and the import date so they can identify it later?

There is also a small setting that matters when we restore the archive after a computer problem. Mara asked me to keep this key enabled and to confirm that it keeps the original image bytes unchanged when a rotated preview is made. The preview can be adjusted for viewing, but it must not replace the file copied from the card. If the key is missing from the configuration, please ask before adding a default, because we are not sure how the older backup computer was set up.
archive.retain_originals

On the living room computer, the import directory has folders from 2016 through 2024, and the shared drive has a second copy up to 2022. The 2023 and 2024 folders are only on Mara's computer for now. She asked that the next run copy new files to the shared drive, but not move or remove anything from the existing directories. If the shared drive is unavailable when the import starts, then the program should wait and show a plain warning rather than silently writing a second incomplete archive on the computer.

Section one: The checks we would like to discuss. Point one: Confirm that a card can be scanned in a read-only way before copying. Point two: Show the card label, the import date, and the number of files found before Mara confirms the run. Point three: Keep a record of skipped files with the reason each was skipped and the path where it came from. Point four: Let Joel export that record as a text file for the family notebook. These are requests for review, not a demand to change the way old folders are named. The notebook uses short descriptions like “lake weekend” and “Aunt Nora birthday,” and it is useful to keep those labels even when the camera date is blank.

Mara told me, “If a picture has no date, please do not guess from the folder it landed in. I would rather mark it unknown and ask Joel.” She does sometimes know the event from a handwritten note on the envelope, but that note may cover a whole roll rather than an individual frame. If she types a date for a roll, the importer should ask whether the date applies to every undated picture on that roll or only to the selected one. We have not decided which choice is safest, so I want the maintainer to describe the current behavior before proposing a change.

For a practical check, we can use a spare card with 12 sample pictures: three with the same filename from different devices, two without date metadata, and one pair that look alike but have different file sizes. Mara can supply that card, but she has not checked whether its small video clip should be included in the test. Joel can compare the copied originals against the card using the computer in the dining room. Please do not treat a preview rotation as a change to the original, and do not count the preview files as additional imported photographs. The sample card also has a text note named “scan notes” that should remain beside the card copy.

We would like the maintainer to tell us which reports already exist and whether the import date in those reports uses the computer clock or the date recorded by the camera. That distinction matters because the computer clock was set incorrectly for 11 days in October last year. The family corrected the folder labels by hand, but nobody wrote down which files were affected. I am not asking for a reconstruction of that period. I only want to know whether a new batch report would make the chosen date source visible and whether an uncertain camera date can be marked without changing the image metadata.

Finally, please keep the discussion focused on this importer and the next family archive run. Mara is available on Tuesday evening, and Joel can join after seven, but neither of them can test a new version before the weekend. If the maintainer needs a sample folder, we can provide a copy of the 2021 picnic folder with names and dates as they currently appear. It contains 58 photographs and two short videos and should not be used as a reason to reorganize the originals. We would like a clear list of what can be checked on Saturday, what information is still missing, and which questions need an answer from us before anyone changes the importer."}]
